Wiskitki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wiskitki, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Wiskitki began after 1793; by 1921, 951 Jews made up over 34% of the town's population, and were deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in February 1941 before most were murdered at Treblinka the following year. The cemetery was established in the first half of the 19th century - synagogue supervision leased the land in 1841 - and until the 1870s also served Jews from nearby Żyrardów. Most tombstones were removed and the fence torn down over the following decades, leaving the site heavily overgrown and hard to access by the early 21st century. About 70 tombstones survive today, the oldest dated 1852, though this represents only about 4% of the burials recorded in historical record books. In 2016, the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage and the ESJF cleaned and fenced the site with concrete, adding a commemorative plaque at the entrance.
